turns.text: hey, can you help me plan this sunday's batch cooking? i want to make two dishes for the week while theo naps. please put the shopping list in table form, i think better in tables
Happy to. A few quick questions so the plan fits: do you have any dishes you already like making, any dietary restrictions, and how much time do you realistically get while Theo sleeps?

ok context. i can make scrambled eggs, boxed pasta and one chili recipe. that's the whole repertoire 🙃 so chili is dish #1 and i need a dead simple second dish. also i'm lactose intolerant, i use oat milk, so nothing that needs real dairy or can swap cleanly. cooking has to fit around the 9, 12:30 and 4 o'clock crib naps, so i get maybe an hour and a half max per nap

Great, that's workable. Since chili is covered, I'd suggest a dairy-free baked chicken and rice casserole as dish #2. It's very forgiving and reheats well.

**Sunday timeline**
- 9:00 nap: prep and brown everything for the chili, start it simmering (it can sit on low while you handle the wake window)
- 12:30 nap: assemble the chicken and rice bake. It's mostly dumping things in a dish, then 45 minutes in the oven
- 4:00 nap: portion both into containers and label them, then clean up

**Chicken and rice bake (dairy-free)**
- Chicken thighs, rice, chicken broth, diced onion, garlic, a bag of frozen mixed vegetables, olive oil, salt, pepper, paprika
- Mix rice, broth, onion, garlic and seasoning in a baking dish, top with chicken and veggies, cover with foil, bake at 375°F for about 45 minutes. No milk or cheese needed. If you ever want it creamier, a splash of unsweetened oat milk works.

What do you use in your chili, so I can build that part of the list?

ground beef, onion, canned kidney beans, canned diced tomatoes, chili powder, cumin, a bell pepper. also i shop saturday mornings at ruiz family market with theo in the carrier so i'd like the list organized in the order of the store, ideally nothing heavy at the bottom of my one-handed haul

Here's a list grouped by store section, so you can work through it with one free hand. I'd guess a typical layout (produce, then meat counter, then canned and dry goods, then frozen). Adjust the order if the market differs.

| Section | Item | Amount | For |
|---|---|---|---|
| Produce | Yellow onions | 3 | both |
| Produce | Bell pepper | 1 | chili |
| Produce | Garlic | 1 head | both |
| Meat counter | Ground beef | 1.5 lb | chili |
| Meat counter | Chicken thighs | 2 lb | bake |
| Canned/dry | Kidney beans | 2 cans | chili |
| Canned/dry | Diced tomatoes | 2 cans | chili |
| Canned/dry | Chicken broth | 1 carton | bake |
| Canned/dry | Long-grain rice | 1 small bag | bake |
| Spices | Chili powder, cumin, paprika | check pantry | both |
| Pantry | Olive oil, salt, pepper | check pantry | both |
| Frozen | Mixed vegetables | 1 bag | bake |
| Frozen/optional | Unsweetened oat milk | only if needed | bake |

Tip: put the cans and rice in the bottom of the bag and the produce on top, and ask for the meat to be packed together so it's easy to unload.

Want a containers and portions guide so the week's dinners are easy to grab?
yes please, thanks. scoreboard: dad 1, dinner 1 so far, going for a repeat

Going for the back-to-back! Here's the portioning plan:

| Dish | Container | Portions | Fridge life |
|---|---|---|---|
| Chili | Medium containers | 4 | 4 days |
| Chicken and rice bake | Medium containers | 4 | 4 days |

- Eat roughly the first four days from the fridge, then freeze the rest flat in freezer bags or containers so they reheat evenly
- Label each container with the dish name and the date you cooked it
- Let everything cool for about 20 minutes before lidding

Good luck on Sunday. Dad 2, dinner 2 is well within reach.
